samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 13. Jumping to Conclusions
samples.relation: Tuomas Manninen uses Endgame's detective work to teach abductive reasoning, inference to the best explanation, as introduced by Charles Peirce, distinguishing it from deduction (Tony Stark is mortal) and induction (Mjolnir-worthiness generalizing to Stormbreaker). He reconstructs Tony's false conclusion that Strange 'gave up the store,' War Machine's wrong guess that Thanos hid the Stones, Cap-2012's mistaken Loki hypothesis upon meeting his future self, and the Ancient One's revised reasoning about Strange surrendering the Time Stone, applying Peter Lipton's actual-versus-potential and likeliest-versus-loveliest distinctions plus five criteria of adequacy (testability, fruitfulness, scope, simplicity, conservatism). Doctor Strange's fourteen-million-futures gambit turns out to combine abduction and deduction into a fallible but insightful plan that only Tony's survival and final snap could fulfill, illustrating Peirce's point that abduction is an instinctive yet rational act of insight.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Johnson uses 'Go God Go's' future of 2546—where Dawkins-style atheism has become a warring religion and otter scientists intone 'Oh my Science!'—to ask whether science and religion genuinely conflict and whether New Atheism is itself a faith. Applying abduction and the four criteria of adequacy, he argues the embellished-story hypothesis beats miracle claims about Jesus (whose legend grew Gospel by Gospel), Sathya Sai Baba, Joseph Smith, and Xenu, that Mr(s). Garrison's 'you can't disprove God' and the show's sarcasm commit an appeal to ignorance, and that Stan's water-into-wine scene with Jesus shows how easily people are fooled. He allows Kuhnian theory change in science but rejects James's will-to-believe for existence claims—the moon whale Willzyx needs evidence—and concludes Parker and Stone are unfair to Dawkins: ending religion would not end violence, but it would remove the easiest justification for it, and some answers are simply true even when unknown.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: An Inexact Science
samples.relation: Demeter argues that Holmes's official self-image as a cold 'reasoning machine' is an ideology that distorts his actual practice: between collecting facts and eliminating impossible scenarios, Holmes is a creator of stories whose 'narrative imagination' invents possible explanations, a phase deduction cannot account for (Peter Lipton's point that Holmesian 'deduction' is not logically valid). Reading 'The Man with the Twisted Lip,' he shows how the same facts (coins in the coat pockets) become different evidence in different narratives until Holmes reconceives Boone and Neville St. Clair as one person. Holmes's preference for the bizarre over the simple, his warning against theorizing before the data, and his claim that his gift is hereditary ('Art in the blood is liable to take the strangest forms') all show detection is closer to art than science, though the scientific persona lends him professional legitimacy and lets him train Scotland Yard.

samples.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
samples.title: James Bond and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abrams explains Peirce's three modes of inference (deduction proves, induction shows, abduction merely suggests) and reconstructs, abduction by abduction, Bond's rapid chain of guesses in The World Is Not Enough: from the odd smell and foam on his fingers to the urea-coated fertilizer bomb he unknowingly delivered, the shared motto 'there's no point living if you can't feel alive' exposing Elektra's alliance with Renard, and her guilty subject-changing. He also covers the negative art: Bond plants false clues with Q's gadgets (the fingerprint re-printer, the cloaked Vanquish) while villains like Carver recode reality by sinking the Devonshire to frame the Chinese, and both sides try to force each other into false abductions. Bond wins because his mind is more playful - Peirce's 'musement', Eco's creative abduction, and an encyclopedic education - making 007 the superior player in what is ultimately a game of chance and strategy.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 9. Why Did Lady Sybil Die
samples.relation: Egg uses the Clarkson versus Tapsell disagreement over Sybil's pre-eclampsia to teach inference to the best explanation, distinguishing deduction (Carson's syllogism about the Australian singer Dame Nellie), induction (Edith's gloomy generalization from her failed suitors), and Peirce's abduction, evaluated via Peter Lipton's twin criteria of likeliness and loveliness. Daisy's numerology linking the Titanic to Pamuk's death and Violet's inference that Edith's Swiss trip hides a pregnancy show loveliness cutting both ways, while Sybil's death tragically vindicates Clarkson's lovelier but less likely diagnosis. The darkest turn is Violet's second-order manipulation: once 'eclampsia plus Robert's misjudgment' threatens her son's marriage, she gets Clarkson to re-weigh the statistics so that 'eclampsia alone' becomes the best explanation of Sybil's death, showing that the best explanation can be engineered.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jones argues that Shawn's 'psychic' act is really hypersensory perception (HSP) - noticing cat fur, fine print, blood spatter - feeding inference to the best explanation (IBE), the natural abductive method Sherlock Holmes mislabels deduction, with Clever Hans and Ilga Kirks as real-world parallels. Applying IBE with Ockham's Razor to the two hypotheses 'he's psychic' versus 'he's hyper-observant,' she concludes the natural explanation should win for everyone: Lassiter's skepticism tracks the evidence, Gus knows better despite believing in ghosts, and Chief Vick shouldn't buy the supernatural story either. Juliet's belief survives only through background supernatural beliefs, a psychic-friendly culture, and ignoring the clues Gus feeds Shawn, which the chapter diagnoses as the same public misunderstanding of the scope and limits of science that keeps most Americans believing in ESP.

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: Kickstarting Inductive Inference
samples.relation: Daniel Wilkenfeld analyzes Veronica's 'magic trick' in the 'One Angry Veronica' juryroom and her season-long bus-crash solution as Peter Lipton's inference to the best explanation: the hypothesis 'Beaver is a killer' wins by consilience (explaining the explosion, the dead rat, Curly Moran, even her chlamydia), simplicity, and completeness. But the criteria face Hume's problem of induction — why think the future will resemble the past, when yesterday's popular girl is today's pariah? — and Descartes's evil demon undermines even what Veronica 'sees,' since Curly Moran could fake a bus crash, leaving no non-circular justification for inferential habits none of us can live without. Following Nelson Goodman, Wilkenfeld concludes the demand for justification is misplaced: what matters is that Veronica reasons consistently, in the juryroom as at the cliff.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
samples.relation: Noël Carroll reconstructs Halloween's Undead iconography from the Celtic Samhain and Pope Gregory's absorption of it into All Hallows' Eve, then poses the paradox that people pay to be terrified by corpse imagery they would flee in a real morgue — odd, given Heidegger's point that the Angst of death is so deep we spend our lives denying it. He tests Ernest Jones's Freudian reading of the nightmare — the vampire revenant as a disguised, disavowed incest wish — and rejects it as a Rube-Goldberg apparatus requiring universal incestuous desire and the whole machinery of the unconscious, when sometimes a zombie is just a zombie and The Fog is simply frightening. His own hypothesis: horror films and Halloween give viewers, especially anxious adolescents, a controlled trial run of fear that eases the meta-fear of fear itself, with Bergson's 'anaesthesis of the heart' explaining why Halloween parody and laughter serve the same emotional-control function as the scares.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: Getting Right with Brian (Just in Case)
samples.relation: Reads Life of Brian through Nietzsche's madman: the crowd's laughter at Brian's market sermons ('consider the lilies... have the birds got jobs?') enacts the death of the cheerless, pathos-soaked God, with Brian as a sincere 'divine idiot' who escapes ressentiment by falling idiotically below the dialectic rather than rising above it as an Übermensch. Bergson's account of the comic — rigidity invisible to its bearer, 'as though wearing the ring of Gyges with reverse effect' — explains why the Pythons' straight men, British class consciousness, and the Roman/British empires ('Romani ite domum,' the centurion's Latin lesson) are funny, and why Britons and Romans can laugh at themselves while Americans cannot. Pivoting from Jorge's war on laughter in Eco's The Name of the Rose, the chapter closes with a Pascal's-wager parody: having laughed at Brian, you have already wagered your immortal soul on God being British — the sort of God who can take a joke.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 4. Is It Immoral to Read Someone to Filth
samples.relation: Birnie stages Alexis Michelle's hurt at the Season 9 body-shaming reads against Bianca Del Rio's 'rolodex of hate' to ask whether reading is immoral. He surveys the philosophical ethics of humor — Plato's Philebus on laughter as malicious delight in others' self-ignorance, Hobbes's 'sudden glory', Schopenhauer on why ridicule hurts, the Stoics' ideal of never laughing, Aristotle's eutrapelia as the golden mean between vulgar buffoon and boor, the Spencer–Freud relief theory, and Bergson's laughter as society's corrective — before endorsing the play theory: reads are consensual mock-aggression, verbal sport honed by marginalized black and Latinx ball culture. From this he derives three guidelines (play signals and consent, timing and audience given the show's younger mainstream viewers, openness to challenge) and concludes Katya's bus-stop read of Roxxxy was acceptable while stereotype reads need care.

samples.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
samples.title: 2. How Can Torture Be This Funny
samples.relation: Asks how a sitcom about torture can be funny and answers with incongruity theory (circus music under Michael's dejection; a comedy set in Hell) plus Bergson's view of comedy as social correction that deflates those who deserve it — Tahani's name-dropping, Michael failing 802 reboots. It centers on 'The Trolley Problem': Michael teleporting Chidi's ethics lesson into real runaway trolleys ('not real, but the pain is') is both incongruous humor and genuine torture, and invoking Bernard Williams shows the real wrongdoer is Michael, who rigged the situation, not Chidi who must choose. Eternal torture, it concludes, only works as endless low-grade everyday crappiness, which is comic in twenty-two-minute doses — and Eleanor's twice-given forgiveness of Michael, after seeing the centuries of torture in Janet's VR device, is the show's real moral marvel.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: The Meta-Fear of Fear
samples.relation: Noel Carroll traces Halloween's Undead imagery to the Celtic Samhain and its Catholic absorption into All Hallows' Eve, then asks the paradox: why do we take pleasure in images of the death that, as Heidegger says, is the deep source of Angst we spend our lives denying? He examines Ernest Jones's Freudian analysis - the vampire as wish-fulfillment disguising an incestuous desire, horror as the price the super-ego exacts - and rejects it as theoretically expensive, invoking the demand for simpler, more economical explanation. His own hypothesis is the 'meta-fear of fear': adolescent viewers (and aging ones) use horror films and the holiday's zombie costumes to test and master fear itself, with parody and Bergson's laughter as companion devices of emotional control - a folk remedy that needs no unconscious to work.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Against Hobbes's view that laughter expresses superiority and Bergson's that comedy humiliates the socially disruptive into conformity, argues that viewers of The Office feel humiliation 'by proxy': Michael Scott is immune to humiliation because his narcissism blocks the minimal condition for feeling it - recognizing he could do wrong (Prison Mike, his MLK name tag while stereotyping Kelly, reneging on the pledge to Oscar's nephew, Carol's rejection at Diwali). We blush, look away, and feel his shame in his place, which transforms neither Michael nor us but reaffirms our own decency, compassion, and grip on values like self-awareness - and the chapter answers the worry that this merely endorses 'Hollywood' values by noting the standards Michael violates (moral sight, honesty with oneself) cross value systems.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 13. Hangings, Shootings, and Other Funny Stuff in 1984
samples.relation: Hietalahti combines Kierkegaard's thesis that the comic lies in contradiction, Plato's warning that laughter is malicious and must be chained by law, and Bergson's account of laughter as social punishment to explain Oceania's humor: the cinema audience laughs at refugees being machine-gunned, citizens clamor for public hangings, and the barroom joke about living in treetops humiliates the old man, because shared fear and hatred set the norms of what counts as funny. Doublethink explains why slogans like 'War is peace' provoke no laughter in Oceania, and the Ministry of Truth's amusement industry shows the Party deliberately weaponizes fun. The upshot is reflexive: Orwell indicts our own unexamined sense of humor, including the slogan that everything may be ridiculed, not merely Oceania's.

samples.book: 218 - The Philosophy of the Coen Brothers
samples.title: Philosophies of Comedy in O Brother, Where Art Thou
samples.relation: McFarland explains the comedy of O Brother through Bergson's 'mechanical encrusted on the living' (the chain-gang pratfall where McGill forgets he is shackled, the toon-like plasticity of the escapees) and Kierkegaard's account of the comic as unresolved contradiction, like men bustling on a sinking ship. He argues the Klan-rally set piece refuses Jamesonian 'pastiche' by grounding its Wizard-of-Oz and Odyssey allusions in real historical guilt, forcing the postmodern aesthete-viewer, as in Kierkegaard's Either/Or, from the aesthetic to the ethical stage. The subverted ending—Penny rejecting the non-bona-fide ring—enacts Kierkegaard's view that marriage is comic because it 'binds' time and acknowledges contradiction rather than resolving it.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 25 Fear of a Black Museum Black Existentialism
samples.relation: Charles Peterson reads the museum scene through Black existentialism and Africana phenomenology: colonial museums freeze African existence in an 'archaic amber' of aesthetic purity, and Killmonger's reclaiming of the mask and questioning of the curator perform a truth-telling that breaks the museum's performance of dominance. Du Bois's double-consciousness explains Killmonger's inseparable Wakandan-and-American two-ness (extended to Nakia and the War Dogs), while Paget Henry's contrast of the DuBoisian subject who oscillates between two 'We's' with Hegel's recognition-seeking subject explains why T'Chaka chooses Wakanda and abandons N'Jobu, and Plato's cave frames Killmonger as dragging Wakanda's comfortable council toward truths 'some truths are too much to bear.' The chapter concludes that Killmonger fails because wearing the mask he embraced negrification rather than shedding it, whereas T'Challa matures from a Hegelian into a DuBoisian subject by opening Wakanda to the world.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: One and Multitudes
samples.relation: Reads Naomi through Latina feminist phenomenology — Ortega's 'multiplicitous subjectivity', Lugones's 'world-traveling', Anzaldúa's borderlands — as one subject inhabiting several incompatible social worlds at once: Belter and Roci crewmate, Marco's former partner and Holden's lover, who experiences Miller's killing of Dresden simultaneously as her captain does and 'as a Belter, Miller wasn't wrong.' Du Bois's double consciousness names her two-ness when the Inaros faction pulls her back into a world she can still slip into 'as if she'd never stopped', and Ashford's list of her identities ('radical, betrayed, hid with the Inners, big hero') shows the borderlands Belters occupy between Inner and Outer worlds. The chapter argues this unsettlement is not a defect but a critical vantage: one stream of experience can carry multiple, conflicting meanings simultaneously, and all of it — no part more than another — is who Naomi is.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Soper tracks Bono's public identity work across three paradigms: pre-modern Irish-Catholic inheritance, including a Du Boisian 'double consciousness' of the colonized Irish; the modernist artist-as-visionary, where Nietzsche, Freud and Marx destabilize the self and the Shalom fellowship nearly ends the band; and the postmodern masks of the Fly, Mirrorball Man and MacPhisto on the Zoo TV media collage, read via Lacan for 'Mofo' and via Baudrillard's simulacra for the 'Even Better than the Real Thing' video with its wax Beatles and cyber-sex imagery. Lyotardian skepticism toward grand ideologies explains the band's refusal of fanaticism in 'Sunday Bloody Sunday' and 'Two Hearts Beat as One'. Soper concludes that Bono fuses all three into a 'Postmodern Christian Pragmatism' that keeps Christian conviction and debt-relief activism while adopting postmodern playfulness without collapsing into ironic detachment.

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
samples.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 70. Jerry Seinfeld as Philosopher The Assimilated Sage of New Chelm
samples.relation: Stern and Gimbel argue that Seinfeld's observational comedy is 'neo-Talmudic': like the rabbis who interpret the fixed text of the Torah, Seinfeld takes an accepted 'given' (shared phenomenological experience, e.g. the milk bit) and generates surprising wisdom by viewing it from an oblique angle. They read Seinfeld's outsider vantage through Du Bois's double consciousness (the assimilated Ashkenazi Jew who sees through two lenses at once) and invoke Derrida's differance as reintegrating Jewish pluralist epistemology into Western thought, with Nietzsche's slave-revolt as an analogy for how Jewish philosophy was made invisible. The sitcom Seinfeld, by contrast, is cast as the modern 'Chelm' joke cycle, parodying that same neo-Talmudic reasoning by pushing local logic (Elaine's Jujyfruits, Schindler's List) into absurdity.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: “I'm in Charge Now, Phasma, I’m in Charge!”
samples.relation: Perez reads Finn through Stuart Hall's account of 'black' as a politically constructed category and Du Bois's 'social heritage of slavery': as the first helmetless Black stormtrooper, Finn simultaneously evokes the Nazi Sturmtruppen and a child enslaved by the First Order, and his self-naming with Poe enacts Hartman's claim that the enslaved must fashion new identities to be free. The chapter then uses colorism, Feagin's white racial frame, and Bloomquist's minstrel studies to argue that Boyega's Finn was sidelined - minimized in marketing, reduced to comic relief and Rose's rebukes, denied his native accent like a linguistic stereotype - wasting the trilogy's most timely story, while Jannah's Company 77 and The Bad Batch hint at the fuller reckoning with stormtrooper slavery Star Wars never attempted.

samples.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
samples.title: Economies of Time in Clockers
samples.relation: Gilmore reads Clockers through DuBois's double-consciousness, arguing the film's dualities—the clockers' street dealing mirroring capitalist 'logic of maximum performance,' kronos versus kairos time, Hyde's commodity versus gift economies, systemic versus personal racism—make white and black viewers alike feel the anguish of Strike and Victor. The Gran Fury as predatory law, the slave-block-style police shakedown watched by Strike's mother, and Rocco seeing only his own reflection in Victor's eye illustrate Heideggerian thrownness and self-love-as-racism. Invoking Peirce's 'evolutionary love' (Radio Raheem's Right Hand/Left Hand speech), Rorty's renarrativization of who counts as 'white,' and Dewey's 'art is more moral than moralities,' Gilmore casts Lee as a pragmatist renarrativizing hate into love.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman uses Buffy's vampire brothel (humans paying vampires to feed on willing victims, as Giles concedes) and Blade's mandatory blood bank as two models of human-vampire coexistence to stage the clash between libertarianism (Nozick, Lomasky, Schmidtz) and welfarism (Singer, Unger, G.A. Cohen). He runs vampire personhood through Nozick's criteria from Anarchy, State, and Utopia — sentience, self-consciousness, rationality, free will, moral personality, soul — and argues no standard includes humans while excluding vampires, applying Singer's equal-consideration-of-suffering principle across kinds of beings. He then extends Singer's obligation-to-aid reasoning (rescuing a drowning child vs. donating to UNICEF) to show welfarism would mandate forced blood transfers or 'blood stamps', and argues via Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules and modern welfare-based anti-immigration politics that the burden of supporting dependents breeds exclusion. Only the libertarian brothel model of voluntary exchange, he concludes, turns vampire-human relations into a positive-sum game in which humans would actually come to recognize vampires as persons.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: So, What Have Philosophers Ever Done for Us
samples.relation: Taylor defends philosophy's bizarre examples against critics like Leon Kass by comparing them to Python's self-reflexive comedy: the 'Complaints' sketch's regress of complaints-about-complaints mirrors how thought experiments make us the audience of our own thinking, as with two coalmine trolley cases that pressure a simple 'minimize pain' utilitarianism toward rule utilitarianism. The 'Police Station' sketch, where it would be better if mad Angus's carnivorous-blancmange story were false, is itself a counterexample to 'always tell the police the truth', and 'The Visitors' stale three-year-old drink invitation undermines the claim that 'inviting in' a fetus creates duties, sharpening Thomson's violinist argument that a right to life does not include a right to another's body. Singer's drowning-child style example and Thomson's violinist show that far-fetched cases clarify practical issues like abortion and famine relief precisely by detaching them from clouding emotion, and the Life of Brian 'What have the Romans ever done for us?' scene supplies the answer: philosophers' examples clarify our views, test them, and are amusing.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman contrasts two pop-culture templates: Buffy's vampire brothel, where willing humans pay vampires for consensual bites (Giles calls the customers 'willing victims'), and Blade's implied government blood bank, where humans are forced to donate. Running Robert Nozick's personhood criteria (sentience, rationality, free will, moral agency, soul) against vampires, he argues no standard admits humans while excluding them, so staking vampires violates rights and, on Singer's suffering-equals-suffering logic, refusing consideration is a kind of speciesism. The welfarist side - Singer and Unger's principle that we must prevent bad at little cost, as in the drowning child - would mandate Blade-style forced blood transfers, but Whitman contends such coercion breeds the very xenophobia (Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules, anti-immigrant welfare politics) that blocks recognizing vampire personhood. Only a libertarian market of voluntary exchange turns human-vampire relations from a zero-sum war into a positive-sum commerce.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Moosa uses the apocalypse as a moral laboratory: since 'murder' is by definition wrongful killing, Carl's shooting of Shane must be judged by his reasoning (saving his father), and Hobbes's state of nature — 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short' — fits Kirkman's world, yet the survivors import morality into it, as when parents mercy-kill their children just as one would turn up a dying child's morphine. Taking up Camus's claim that suicide is the one truly serious philosophical problem, he argues our world is nearly as bad as the zombie landscape, so consistency commits comfortable readers to the same duty of aid (helping sufferers rather than opting out) that justifies the survivors' fighting on. Finally he argues procreation is the worst thing survivors can do — nonexistent children cannot suffer, so Lori's pregnancy and Glenn and Maggie's crib plans are immoral, and adopting existing children as Andrea and Dale did is the consistent course, an obligation that transfers to our world right now.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Skyler King uses the Gang's inheritance war over their dead mother's possessions as a metaphor for greed versus need, pressing our duties to those in extreme suffering. Peter Singer's utilitarian argument - prevent bad without sacrificing anything of comparable significance, absolute poverty is bad, therefore we ought to give - makes charity a requirement rather than a nicety, condemning Dennis's luxury purchases and crowning Bruce Mathis, the one character who consistently donates, as the utilitarian exemplar. Nel Noddings's feminist ethics of care counters that we owe help only to those within reach whose good we can see 'completed in the other' - so Mac and Dennis wronged Charlie by refusing him shelter in the recession, but owe nothing to children overseas - and the chapter weighs Dee-style objections that this licenses caring only when inconvenienced, closing with the question 'is it always sunny in your Philadelphia?'

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Moosa treats Kirkman's world as a moral laboratory: the apocalypse approximates Hobbes's state of nature ('solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'), yet Rick's search for his family shows survivors import morality into it, and Carl's killing of Shane is judged by reasoning rather than the act of killing itself. Taking Camus's claim that suicide is the only serious philosophical problem, the chapter argues the survivors' best justification for continuing is reducing others' suffering, and consistency then imposes the same duty on comfortable readers to help real-world sufferers rather than reserving aid for photogenic disasters. It concludes that Glenn and Maggie's wish to conceive at the prison is the worst thing survivors can do, since non-existent children cannot suffer while existing orphans (like the children Andrea and Dale adopted) have prior moral claims, an argument that applies to couples in our world too.

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 8. Saints and Superheroes
samples.relation: Malloy uses the two heroes to explain supererogation - Urmson's "Saints and Heroes" puzzle of acts that are praiseworthy but not obligatory, like Batman rushing into burning buildings while Jimmy Olsen is under no duty to follow. Against the utilitarian and deontological denials that anything goes beyond duty (Singer's argument that Clark Kent's designer glasses are money he owes to charity, and Susan Wolf's Loving and Rational Saints whose lives, like Batman's broken retirements in The Dark Knight Returns and Batman Beyond, leave no room for anything worth living), he adopts Raz's view that a duty can be overridden by the moral reason of grave personal risk. Hence Batman's nightly risk-taking is a genuinely heroic choice, while Superman's powers make saving others morally required - so Batman is more truly a hero and Superman "just a good person with the powers of a living god."

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Wishing and Dogmatism
samples.relation: Matthew Pierlott argues Colbert the satirist conflates two things his character, Stephen, merges: truthiness (trusting gut and heart over external authorities like dictionaries) and bullshit in Frankfurt's exact sense - speech indifferent to truth, which Pierlott finds in Hillary Clinton's dismissal of economists on the gas-tax holiday and likens to Steve Careill's habitual pleasantries versus Jon Stewart's honesty and Stephen's lies. He defends gut and heart as evidence-bearing tools - knowing a candidate's 'heart' from character evidence (the Westmoreland Ten Commandments interview), gut intuitions as unconsciously processed experience, and choosing which of the two Cheneys (1994 quagmire prophet or 2003 liberators booster) to trust - so in an information-saturated democracy truthiness is a necessary part of any orientation toward truth. The real enemy is dogmatism, the 'Dark Side of Truthiness' that cuts off future evidence, while wishful thinking kept modest (optimism that people are honest) can even be beneficial, a Jamesian willing-to-believe.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Our Distinguished Panel of Incomparable Geniuses
samples.relation: Fuller's finale casts Francis Bacon's scientific method as an inquisitorial trial designed to manage bullshit: everyone may produce it, provided a third-party judge frames a 'crucial experiment' that decides between the parties — a vision only partially realized by the Royal Society and later positivism, and tempered by Karl Popper's open-society point that all may bullshit to their heart's content given agreement on how to clean up after it. He tests the model on the Lomborg affair (initially found 'scientifically dishonest', then acquitted on appeal because politicized research is the environmental norm), on Zola's J'Accuse and Galileo's vindication in Newton's Principia as productive bullshit, and on his own service as expert witness: McLean v. Arkansas cut through creationist and evolutionist bullshit with a neutral definition of science, while Kitzmiller v. Dover adopted a 'methodological naturalism' custom-built to exclude Intelligent Design — justice losing out to the side whose bullshit is piled higher and deeper.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Blessing and Marren mine Stewart's two interviews with Harry Frankfurt to work out the lie/bullshit distinction: liars like Edwards, Weiner and Clinton know and care about the truth they distort, while bullshitters, from Travelodge PR stunts to subprime lenders, are indifferent to truth in service of selling, which is why Frankfurt calls bullshit the more corrosive force. They take up Stewart's Socratic questioning of whether political spin is a subset of bullshit, and answer that spinners, unlike bullshitters, must know the truth in order to color it, making spin closer to lying in attitude, tolerated because Spin Alley agrees not to call bullshit on it. samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_

samples.relation: Borrowing Harry Frankfurt's move of philosophically defining a colloquial term (as Frankfurt did for 'bullshit'), it defines a 'dick' as someone who willfully disregards others' needs and argues Superman is one: the vending-machine thought experiment shows he could rescue a sinking school bus in less time than it takes Clark to buy a chocolate bar, so saving people at little or no cost to himself is obligatory, not supererogatory. Batman, who risks his mortal life and seeks out strangers to save, is 'not a dick' and wins the round.

samples.title: Trust and Truth
samples.relation: Kellen builds successive definitions of lying from ATLA cases: Aang's invented Jin Wei and Wei Jin story in 'The Great Divide' is a plain lie, Toph's 'How could I possibly play? samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: And in the End
samples.relation: Irwin and addictions specialist Lombardo ask where comic inspiration comes from, using Socrates' discovery that poets do not know the meaning of their own work, Hume's account of creativity as recombining materials of experience, and Nietzsche's point that inspiration is really continuous production sifted by judgment, to explain why Belushi and Farley treated cocaine and alcohol as muses. They contrast Belushi's fatal 'I use drugs' hubris, which no one around him challenged, with Farley's genuine twelve-step recovery, three sober years, and relapses. Stuart Smalley's affirmations, which bullshit himself into feeling 'good enough,' spoof recovery culture's cliches while Farley's story shows what actual recovery demands, ending with the advice to look elsewhere for the muse.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: The Death of Death
samples.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

samples.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
samples.title: War and Its Fictional Recovery On-Screen Narrative Management of Death in The Big Red One and The Thin Red Lin
samples.relation: Bronfen takes Freud's 'Thoughts for the Times on War and Death' (life 'recovers its full content' when war forces us to believe in death) and his theory of the death drive and the uncanny double as a template for how war films manage mortality through fiction. In Fuller's The Big Red One, the nameless Sergeant's guilt-driven distinction between killing and murder, his Nazi double Schroeder, and the compulsively repeated stabbing scene at the crucifix let the hero convert contingent slaughter into a restitutive story where survival is 'the only glory,' echoing Freud's Eros–Thanatos struggle. In Malick's The Thin Red Line, Private Witt splits not into warlike and peacetime selves but into bodily and spiritual presence, embracing death as transcendence into 'shining light' that doubles the light of cinema itself. samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: The Possibility of a Non-Repressive Civilization
samples.relation: Simon Clark reads Romero's four Dead films through Freud's Civilization and Its Discontents: the zombie is the return of the repressed, the ripped-out instinctual life of a civilization that demands work, and it multiplies exactly as humans (Stephen defending the mall, Ben fighting Mr. Cooper) lapse into unlawful self-gratification. The bite unites Eros and Thanatos - an erotic, engorged cannibalism that also regresses victims to rotting matter, which Clark glosses with Creed's vagina dentata. He then argues Day of the Dead's beach ending (John fishing, Sarah at peace) stages Marcuse's non-repressive civilization where work becomes play and liberated sexuality rejoins Eros, while Land of the Dead goes further: the evolved, tool-using zombies led by Big Daddy are the martyrs who actually found Marcuse's impossible pleasurable community, leaving living humans still fenced inside repression.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Sets up Sons of Anarchy as a Hamlet retelling — Jax the prince, Clay the Claudius who murdered John Teller and married Gemma, Tara a gutsier Ophelia — and reads it through Freud and Ernest Jones's Hamlet and Oedipus: Jax's protest that he 'untwisted my mommy thing a long time ago,' his toleration of Gemma's meddling, and the Season 4/5 finale tableaux where Gemma displaces Tara at his side betray an unresolved Oedipus complex. Freud's three agencies get bodies: Clay as pure Id (beating Gemma in 'Hands'), Tara as Superego, Jax as the mediating Ego, with SAMCRO itself a collective Id worshipped in its 'chapel.' Oral and anal-stage fixations explain the Sons' chain-smoking, recklessness, and defiance of authority, while the Id's civil war between libido and the death drive plays out in Gemma's post-beating sex binge and Jax's unconscious pleasure in killing.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: Moral Man in the Dark City Film Noir, the Postwar Religious Revival, and The Accused
samples.relation: Palmer nuances the 'dark mirror' theory of noir by recovering a redemptive subgroup, reading Dieterle's The Accused through the postwar religious revival and the writings of Reinhold Niebuhr and Erich Fromm. Where Lang's The Woman in the Window only chastens its professor via a dream, The Accused stages a genuinely penitential arc: repressed psychology professor Wilma Tuttle kills the aggressive student Bill in panic, then is therapeutically forced to relive the crime (at the prizefight and in the reenactment) until love with lawyer Warren Ford delivers her from 'separateness.' Palmer argues this patriarchal, therapeutic 'conversion'—glamorizing Loretta Young out of her mannish disguise—reconfigures Niebuhr's taming of passion and Fromm's account of love as a decision, heralding a coming 'culture of narcissism.'

samples.book: 124 - Tom Petty and Philosophy - We Need to Know
samples.title: 10. Change of Heart
samples.relation: Auxier names Petty the master of "liminal moments" when something is finally seen for what it is (the betrayed lover's realization behind "You Got Lucky," the unknown pain of "American Girl"), then stages the 1929 Davos debate between Cassirer's humane, Goethe-reading phenomenology and Heidegger's Angst before the abyss, being-toward-death, and the "moment of vision." samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 18. Iron Man’s Choice to Die
samples.relation: Argues Tony's death in Endgame is best explained three ways: via Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives (Tony oscillates between the cabin family-life drive and the risk-seeking death drive that takes him aboard the donut ship in Infinity War and has him lay down to die with Nebula), via Camus's absurd (like Sisyphus, Tony creates subjective meaning by choosing — Pepper, Morgan, and finally the snap itself, 'Part of the journey is the end'), and via consequentialism (the snap as a desirable consequence, contrasting Infinity War's deontological 'We don't trade lives' with Endgame's 'whatever it takes'). samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Christopher Ketcham narrates a night listening to Dear Heather during a café blackout, in which darkness becomes Eugene Minkowski's 'lived space' - more personal than light, with auditory space as its own dark space - and Cohen's voice leads him down into a shared funk of loss and depression. samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Epilog
samples.relation: Nicolas Floury reads the entire film as the single dream of a neurotic subject — Cobb asleep on the plane, every character assembled from fellow passengers and airport figures — in which he works through the Lacanian conflict where the neurotic 'does not desire what he wants and does not want what he actually desires': Cobb wants to keep living with Mal ('In my dreams we are still together') while wishing to complete her mourning. The dream levels are reinterpreted as stages of Freudian dream-work: level 1 ruled by desire, level 2 where the counter-desire and Ariadne-as-double intervene, the snow fortress war as the internal battle climaxing when Cobb shoots Mal, and the limbos as melancholic self-enclosure — 'a life without desire, a life under the seal of death.' samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Young argues that South Park is perceived as dangerous for exactly the reasons Socrates was tried and executed in Plato's Apology: both 'corrupt the youth' by mocking religion, questioning authority, and exposing that the supposed teachers (Mr. Garrison's flip-flopping creationism, Mrs. Broflovski's moral panics, the 'Death' boycott of Terrance and Phillip) do not know what they think they know. He diagnoses Cartman as an Eichmann figure whose banal, thoughtless evil—feeding Scott Tenorman his parents, torturing Muslims with farts—consists in the inability to think from another's standpoint, while Kyle and Stan's friendship embodies Arendt's dialogic thinking and Aristotle's mean between ideological extremes, as when they see both the merit and the smugness of hybrid drivers in 'Smug Alert'. Freud's theory that jokes break through repression explains why the show's vulgarity is essential rather than gratuitous: it verbalizes what culture silences so that it can be thought through, making South Park a Socratic gadfly rather than a corrupter.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: The Horizon of Disenchantment Film Noir, Camus, and the Vicissitudes of Descent
samples.relation: Alan Woolfolk reads noir through Weber's disenchanted world and Charles Taylor's cultural horizons, arguing the noir protagonist can neither resist the darkness like Conrad's Marlow nor fully embrace it like Coppola's Willard, remaining trapped between times in an ethically irrational universe. He contrasts Camus, who counters disenchantment with an ethic of honesty grounded in a Rousseauian benign nature (The Stranger's Meursault) and with the Baudelairean dandy as aesthetic model, against noir protagonists (Neff, Marlowe, the Swede, Scottie Ferguson) whose 'banked fires' fail and who lose self-possession. Drawing on Freud's id as 'a cauldron full of seething excitations,' he argues the femme fatale drags the protagonist downward into the timeless unconscious where anything is possible (Noah Cross's incest in Chinatown, the radioactive box in Kiss Me Deadly, Body Heat's Ned Racine), and reads noir as backward- and downward-looking through Palmer/Bakhtin's chronotope.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 4. How Possible Is the Impossible Girl
samples.relation: Smith asks how one Clara can exist as Oswin the converted Dalek, a Victorian governess, and a present-day nanny, and answers with philosophy of mind: after the real Clara steps into the Doctor's timeline on Trenzalore, the 'echoes' are best understood as manifestations within the Doctor's own subconscious, read through Freud's dream interpretation and id-ego-superego (the echoes act as his conscience) and Jung's archetypes, collective unconscious, individuation, and synchronicity—her name meaning clarity, her red wardrobe marking the copies, and the leaf of 'The Rings of Akhaten' as the meaningful coincidence that produced her. Aristotle's Categories frames what Oswin still shares with humanity after Dalek conversion, and the soufflé-is-the-recipe line together with social-cognition research on multiple selves supports the conclusion that the Claras are metaphysically the same person despite different bodies and roles—making the 'Impossible Girl' possible.

samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Daniel Leonard takes CharDee MacDennis, the Gang's three-level drinking game, as an unconscious confession read through Freud's structural model. The 'Mind' level - grudge trivia like 'Denis is asshole. Why Charlie hate?' and drawing-guessing 'based solely on feel' - runs on the id and the pleasure principle; the 'Body' level of darts, kennels, and the no-cursing rule is restraint, properly the ego's job of deferring gratification (which only Dennis's manipulative D.E.N.N.I.S. System grotesquely exercises); and the 'Spirit' level of Emotional Battery and Public Humiliation externalizes the superego's guilt and ego-ideal, with Frank as the all-seeing punishing father. The Gang's psychology is backwards - their 'Mind' level tests exactly what is not conscious - and their over-strong superegos surface in rationalization and the Black Card's coin flip, while smashing the losers' idealized game pieces enacts a wishful symbolic patricide.

samples.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger

It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.
