samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Paweł Dobrosielski and Marcin Napiórkowski read Flowers for Hitler as Cohen's answer to Adorno's dictum that to write poetry after Auschwitz is barbaric - Cohen writes poetry that self-consciously knows it comes after the end of poetry. Using Freud's distinction between the vocabulary and grammar of dreams, they show the collection is assembled from a small repertoire of recurring images (ovens, ashes, telephones, radios, green grass, Nazi names) whose awkward normality expresses repression: life goes on as if nothing had happened. Arendt's banality of evil, born of the Eichmann trial, is directly alluded to in 'All There Is to Know about Adolf Eichmann,' and the book ends by universalizing Holocaust memory - the poet waking with a number on his forearm, feeling like victim and perpetrator alike - until the grass itself is grown on ashes and every flower is a flower for Hitler.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Argues against the obvious reading that Larry is a rule-breaker: properly analyzed, he is a dedicated rule-follower, since a good rule-follower need only accept the legitimacy of some rules and consistently follow the ones he accepts. Bekka Williams works through cases like Rachel's ski-lift jump versus Jewish law in 'The Ski Lift,' the moving 10:30 pm phone cutoff in 'The Wire,' and Larry's rejection of his mother's tattoo-driven reburial in 'The Special Section' to distinguish breaking a rule you accept from rejecting a rule's legitimacy altogether. Kant supplies the point that duty is only visible when it frustrates self-interest (Larry absorbing the cost of his own waiting-room rule in 'The Interior Decorator,' refusing to fire the Tourette's chef), while J.J.C. Smart's attack on 'rule-worship' explains why Larry rejects purposeless rules like the drive-thru walking ban and the one-year wedding-gift cutoff. The underlying justification is the Golden Rule: the water bottle in 'The Doll,' the caviar allotment, and even the stolen memorial flowers in 'The Ida Funkhouser Roadside Memorial' are defended as fairness and reciprocity, leaving the jacket money in 'The Korean Bookie' as the single admitted counterexample.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: If I Were a Carpenter
samples.relation: Butler asks what makes an activity work, testing the market definition against Socrates' refusal of fees, Aristotle's Politics, Arendt's labor/work/action distinction, Eva Kittay's care work, and the split between extrinsic and intrinsic value. He reads Cash's catalog through it: "One Piece at a Time" (the Detroit line worker stealing a Cadillac he builds but cannot afford), "Get Rhythm" (the shoeshine boy singing through menial labor), "I Never Picked Cotton" (escaping work into an empty identity), "Let Him Roll" and "Southern Accents," and the San Quentin monologue after "Wreck of the Ol' 97" where Cash refuses to be told what to play before inmates. The chapter closes by lining up Kant's categorical imperative, Jesus' Golden Rule, and Rawls's veil of ignorance: nobody would choose a society of company-store wage slavery without knowing they were not the worker, and Cash, knowing he stood on the stage rather than in the cellblock, used his freedom to side with prisoners and carpenters anyway.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Part III Endless Forms Most Beautiful
samples.relation: Muntersbjorn argues that freedom comes in kinds and degrees and that selves are social fictions sustained by others, building on Annette Baier's claims that we are 'second persons' whose self-consciousness and freedom grow out of childhood interaction and mutual cross-examination. She reads the hosts' selective ignoring ('that doesn't look like anything to me') as Baier's dangerous art of self-deception, and contrasts Descartes' solitary introspection (hats and coats that may cover automata) and Russell's analogy-based answer to the problem of other minds with the hosts' deliberately scripted interpersonal checks that keep them from questioning their reality. Plato's Meno statues of Daedalus (opinion 'fastened up' into knowledge) frame hosts as property whose freedom is a matter of degree, and the chapter closes that if artificial beings are ever to become persons they must be treated as second persons first - the Golden Rule applied to the park.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
samples.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter models court intrigue as game theory: games of incomplete information over Joffrey's legitimacy, the predictability of honorable opponents like Barristan Selmy, and Catelyn's reverse induction from the seemingly 'irrational' attack on Bran to deduce that Jaime threw him. Tyrion is the star player, converting one-shot death sentences into repeated games - recruiting Bronn as his champion at the Eyrie, buying off the mountain clans with Lannister arms - and showing how 'A Lannister always pays his debts' works as strategic reputation. Against Plato's view of love as the madness that ruins rational play (Maester Aemon's 'love is the bane of honor'), the chapter uses Nietzsche's 'drop of reason in madness' to argue that lovers' merged interests expand rationality itself, culminating in a Golden Rule upgraded to 'understand others as they understand themselves.'

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents because they meet Aristotle's test of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgment that 'evildoers... taste better') and retain free will, since their blood-lust is a craving not a compulsion and Louis's rat diet in Interview with the Vampire, like Angel's in Buffy, proves an alternative exists. TASTE, full potential, and spiritual peace all fail to justify human blood, because killing a person brings more unnecessary suffering than killing a rat, the same suffering-based principle that condemns factory farming. The 'cold clammy consistency' punchline: since humans need not eat meat, condemning vampire blood-drinkers while dining on chicken, pork, and beef is hypocrisy, because we are vampiric too and only our choice of which life to ingest separates the monstrous from the virtuous.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Cold Clammy Consistency
samples.relation: Wayne Yuen argues vampires are moral agents - rational by Aristotle's standard of practical wisdom (Lestat's investments and his judgments about evildoers tasting better) and free despite their blood-craving, since craving is a strong preference, not the compulsion of the heroin addict or the castaway drinking seawater. Since animal blood is a viable alternative (Louis's rats, Angel and Spike's butcher's blood), the justifications for drinking human blood - taste, reaching full potential, spiritual peace - all fail against the principle that a world with less unnecessary suffering is better. Then the consistency argument turns on us: factory-farmed meat inflicts unnecessary suffering for the sake of taste while vegetarianism is fully viable, so condemning vampires while eating chicken is inconsistent - we as human beings are vampiric.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Allaire argues walkers have no moral value and can be killed without remorse: a Bentham-style act-utilitarian tally favors killing any walker, and, following Kant, genetic humanity is neither necessary nor sufficient for membership in the moral community. Applying Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, he shows walkers lack pain response (Hannah's severed half still dragging itself at Rick), language, planning (Glenn's gun-bag mission versus aimless shuffling), and self-reflection, so as beings incapable of duty they can have no rights. Morgan's inability to shoot his walker-wife and Rick's 'I'm sorry this happened to you' illustrate Kant's 'duality of the human situation' — we irrationally project personhood onto former people — and our hesitation is precisely the walkers' greatest advantage.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 7 The Bourgeoisie and the Blacks
samples.relation: The chapter sets business - the US bourgeoisie whose privileged position Charles Beard read into the Constitution and which survived the Jacksonian and New Deal challenges by breaking labor through Taft-Hartley, right-to-work laws and the PATCO lockout, its solidarity secured while worker solidarity was undercut by what Marx called the Achilles heel of racism - against blacks as the paradigmatic powerless, shut out of every power base since slavery, which the chapter treats with Baptist and Marx's 1846 letter as a totalitarian system of super-exploited, tortured labor that built American capitalism, its neo-slavery progeny (Blackmon) pauperizing the black community under Dred Scott's 'subordinate and inferior class of beings'. It then narrates black counter-power base by base: the abolitionist interracial coalition wielding charisma (Douglass, Nat Turner, John Brown), information, morality and religion; the NAACP era and King's fusion of charisma, church religion, Myrdal's An American Dilemma and televised nonviolent provocation against Bull Connor's violence, contested by Malcolm X, SNCC and the Black Panthers; and a post-civil-rights scorecard showing a wealth base 94.2 percent white, persistent education and media gaps, constrained black officials from mayors to the symbolic Obama presidency, and a captive but potentially leveraged black vote in a 'Sisyphean' struggle.

samples.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Shea argues the Underwoods' rise is structurally guaranteed rather than far-fetched, surveying democracy's critics: Plato's Republic Books 8-9 has the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decay through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, where a 'protector'-tyrant like Frank exploits the drones and the people's love of freedom (Russo as the prototypical democratic soul, Tusk as the oligarch-in-fact), while the tyrant ends fear-ridden and friendless — precisely Frank's Season 3. Hobbes and Hegel then reverse the verdict, arguing monarchy aligns the ruler's private interest with the public good and lets a people will as one instead of a formless mass — the insight Tom Yates has about voters identifying with the Underwoods as people — and Marx reframes it economically: SanCorp, Tusk, and Feng are the capitalist structure, and Frank's AmWorks, entitlement cuts, and nationalization threats show self-interested politicians siding with a growing proletariat. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government supplies the democratic reply — responsiveness, better information, and citizen participation mean an Underwood cannot last if we keep fair elections, a free press, and real checks.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues the Underwoods' success is not far-fetched fiction but the structural outcome four critics of democracy predict. Plato's Republic supplies the spine: the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decays through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, whose love of freedom invites the tyrant — Peter Russo with his random desires is the democratic soul, Frank the tyrannical soul ruled by one illicit appetite, doomed to the fear and friendlessness Book 9 describes (which Season 3 delivers). Hobbes and Hegel then explain why monarchy may beat popular rule (the monarch's private interest aligns with the public's; the monarch lets a people will as one), and Marx reframes the whole show economically — SanCorp, Tusk and Feng as capitalists, the laid-off shipyard workers as proletariat, and AmWorks as self-interested politicians flirting with expropriation. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government gives the democratic reply — elections force responsiveness, participation educates citizens — so the burden falls on viewers to keep elections fair, the press free, and checks on unscrupulous politicians effective.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Answers The New Yorker's claim that the American Office 'doesn't care about class' by reading it through Marx: capital's growth logic and surplus value explain the degraded office labor the show depicts (Stanley's 'run-out-the-clock type of situation' truck unloading, Pam's tepid watercolors, Roy's 'unloading trucks without meaning', Ryan's rejected assembly line), while the salaried masses' class position survives precisely as unnamable and denied - Michael's botched condo purchase, his fury at Ryan's business-school ambition, and Prison Martin's observation that office and prison are both 'doing the same thing every day'. Drawing on Kracauer, the chapter argues the show's comedy walks between distraction and awakening, and ends with Walter Benjamin's 'authentic humanity' located in the gap between professional and private life: Michael's failures make him an unwitting critique of the system that produced him.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves. The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

samples.book: 020 - Poker and Philosophy - Pocket Rockets and Philosopher Kings
samples.title: Poker and Philosophy
samples.relation: Belliotti tells of busting 'Pickle Puss' with flopped queens and of tight 'Howard the Vest' paying off his flopped full house to ask whether Marx's diagnoses — alienation in four forms, exploitation of surplus value, and false consciousness spread through the ideological superstructure by the economic base — condemn poker. He argues no: unlike coerced factory labor, poker is freely chosen creative activity that energizes our species-being like an absorbed artist, as Doyle 'Texas Dolly' Brunson's road-gambler career and his famous ten-deuce full-house call against Jessie Alto at the 1976 WSOP (and the 1980 loss to Stu Ungar's gutshot) show. Poker may still launder capitalist ideology — antes that lure investment, zero-sum rivalry, rugged individualism — but the owner-worker exploitation Marx feared has no equivalent at an equal-buy-in table.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Uses 'The Last of the Meheecans' to argue that Marx's account of labor-power needs race built into it: once Butters is mistaken for a Mexican immigrant 'Mantequilla', the couple who hit him hand him Windex and a leaf blower and he sings 'Work, Mexican, work', showing how racialization assigns his labor a demeaned value. The episode's conflicting stereotypes (lazy shiftless 'Meheecans' versus the hard-working backbone of service labor) and the mass 'Orgullo de Mantequilla' migration home reveal a super-exploited population. The author then recovers Marx's own writings on Polish and Irish liberation, American slavery, and Lincoln's reelection ('labor in the white skin cannot emancipate itself where in the black skin it is branded') to show that for Marx, racial and national domination were always obstacles to working-class freedom.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Ewing reads Cameron as a Marxist: Cyberdyne's profit-driven reverse-engineering of the recovered Terminator arm, Dyson's alienated labor ('Don't ask'), and U.S. militarism absorbing Cyber Research Systems develop Skynet as capitalism's 'final contradiction,' in which the drive for destructive, labor-replacing technology converges with the profit motive to threaten humanity. Sarah and John are useful to the resistance only when they exit wage labor - waitress to warrior, ATM hacking instead of work - dramatizing Marx's claim that liberation requires transcending class positions. Yet technology itself is neutral and reclaimable: the reprogrammed T-101 learning 'I know now why you cry' shows even killing machines can be humanized for liberation, and the saga ends where Marx does - not interpreting the world but changing it.

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: P A R T F O U R
samples.relation: Four Part Four essays beyond ethics. Aaron Meskin asks whether Watchmen is literature at all, testing definitions from Beardsley, Eagleton, Lamarque/Olsen and Hirsch in the Socratic 'what is X?' way, and concludes the question is indeterminate because comics are a hybrid art form — though the book's literary allusions (Shelley's 'Ozymandias,' Blake's 'Tyger,' Burroughs) deserve literary appreciation regardless. Sarah Donovan and Nick Richardson read the two Silk Spectres through three feminisms: Sally and Laurie as liberal feminists (Wollstonecraft, Mill) who fight crime, their hypersexual costumes as Irigaray-style subversive mimicry of gender stereotypes that risks reinforcing them (the Silhouette's expulsion exposing the heterosexual norm), the Comedian's attempted rape exposing 'she asked for it' attitudes, and Laurie as Beauvoir's woman in bad faith, living out her mother's fantasies until she finally names and dresses herself. Robert Arp uses Hooded Justice and Captain Metropolis's closeted relationship to dismantle 'homosexuality is unnatural' arguments — the ideal-function view would condemn the infertile too, and Hume's is-ought point undermines the procreation argument — before defending gay marriage against slippery-slope and parenting objections. Taneli Kukkonen maps Kierkegaard's stages onto the Comedian's mocking irony (hiding even his paternity of Laurie and his Kennedy confession as jokes) and Rorschach's deeper humor of the ethical stage, a knight of resignation whose 'never compromise, not even in the face of Armageddon' expects nothing back from the world.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Tests moral relativism against absolutism through Enterprise's "Cogenitor": Trip's liberation of the Vissian third-sex being - secretly scanning its brain, naming it Charles, teaching it to read - ends in its suicide, and the chapter asks whether Trip's judgments track rational moral truth or are Humean after-the-fact rationalizations of disgust, since on Hume's view reason is the slave of the passions and is/ought are separate. Kant's categorical imperative (the cogenitor used merely as a means of reproduction) and Aquinas's natural law are offered as absolutist resources on Trip's side, while Phlox voices a Benedict-style "morally good is just habitual" relativism and Archer concludes "we didn't come out here to play God", prefiguring the Prime Directive. The chapter lands on Mary Midgley's rejection of moral isolationism via her tsujigiri example and Quark's "we're better than you" speech to Sisko: cross-cultural judgment is possible, but only after understanding, and not on the first day of first contact.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Robert Arp's gallery matches each Gang vice - dishonesty, egoism, selfishness, greed, pettiness, ignorance, laziness - to real-life scumbags from Nixon, Stephen Glass, and Janet Cooke to Charles Ponzi, Bernie Madoff, Crassus, the Empress Dowager Cixi, Imelda Marcos, and the Darwin Awards, and it opens with the chapter's philosophical spine: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Book II of Plato's Republic, which predicts that even an upstanding person with the power to act unseen would seduce, steal, and murder - exactly the question the Gang's mostly unpunished antics keep staging. Against the ethical egoist's argument that because everyone is self-interested everyone should be (Vanderbilt's 'the public be damned'), the chapter deploys the is-ought point - children are naturally selfish without therefore deserving to be - alongside mothers, Mother Teresa, and 9/11 first responders, concluding that egoism is at most an admixture in every action, with Lord of the Flies as the reductio of universal egoism.

samples.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
samples.title: James Bond and Philosophy
samples.relation: Kowalski explains yin-yang cosmology through the Yi Ching and Shu Ching - opposing forces in dynamic harmony, each containing the seed of its opposite, with excess of either bringing destruction - and applies it to the Brosnan-era films, reading Bond himself as the yang force of action. The films improved, he argues, by strengthening yin: Wai Lin as Bond's equal partner in the handcuffed motorcycle chase of Tomorrow Never Dies (each watching the road the other cannot see), Judi Dench's M as the corrective to Admiral Roebuck's hawkish yang ('the advantage is that I don't always have to think with them'), and Elektra King as a genuine yin villainess rather than a damsel. He ends with a Humean caveat that deriving moral conclusions from the natural order is logically suspect, yet endorses the cosmology's practical advice - balance and harmony between opposing forces - as the reason the new millennium Bond films are better.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 5. Every Lonely Monster Needs a Companion
samples.relation: Gadsden asks why a near-omnipotent Time Lord needs companions at all and tests four hypotheses against his solo meltdowns—executing Solomon in 'Dinosaurs on a Spaceship,' nearly murdering Jex in 'A Town Called Mercy,' and declaring himself 'Time Lord Victorious' in 'The Waters of Mars.' He rejects the Lord Acton power-corrupts hypothesis via Glaucon's ring story in Plato's Republic, since powerless companions offer no threat of reprisal or dishonor, and qualifies J.J. Sylvia's care-ethics 'empathetic link' because the Doctor cares for non-human species like the Star Whale too. He favors two answers: Hume's fact/value gap as a millennium-long moral myopia ('I can't see it anymore,' the deleted 'Flesh and Stone' confession), and Aristotle's point in the Nicomachean Ethics that only virtuous friends—moral peers who mirror us—can expose the Doctor's blind spots, like his 'God Complex.'

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 15. The C-Word
samples.relation: Works through the ethics of cloning and genetic selection, starting with the objection that such technologies are "unnatural": that reasoning commits the naturalistic fallacy, since following Hume you can't get an ought from an is, and human ingenuity (roads, eyeglasses, IVF) is itself part of nature. Using Nietzsche's Genealogy account of master morality — good as the noble traits of intelligence, beauty, and strength — the chapter asks whether parents would then be obliged to engineer better children, while warning where trait-selection slides: Nazi eugenics, racist trait-lists (both Leda and Castor are white and conventionally attractive), and "abilism" against the deaf. It concludes that cloning itself is not evil: Projects Leda and Castor are immoral not because they clone but because they treat clones as mere means to an end, in Kant's sense, and trample their autonomy.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Pigliucci argues the gang is funny because their scientistic worldview misfires in ordinary life: Howard's Drake-equation-derived 'Wolowitz coefficient,' Sheldon's friendship algorithm that Howard must rescue from an infinite loop, and Leonard's 'bio-social exploration' kiss experiment with Leslie all fail because courtship and friendship resist quantification. Tracing scientism's appeal to the Cartesian method of reductionism, he criticizes E.O. Wilson's Consilience, Sam Harris's science of morality (defending Hume's distinction between empirical facts and values), and the Churchlands' eliminative materialism — the tequila sunrise and the rock wall's qualitative feel escaping the neuro-reductive gaze. Sheldon's chocolate-based operant conditioning of Penny and the Tuskegee syphilis study show why science needs ethical evaluation from outside itself.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: Bringing Balance to the Force
samples.relation: Harter argues that Revenge of the Sith manipulates audiences into fearing the medical technology that saves Anakin on Mustafar, portraying his prosthetic transformation into Vader as horrifying when in real bioethical terms saving a burn victim with ventilators, feeding tubes, and prosthetics is something we applaud. He diagnoses Lucas's framing as the naturalistic fallacy (what is natural is good), grounded in Hume's is-ought gap, and flags the mirror-image 'technological fallacy' of assuming enhancement like General Grievous's cyborg body must be good. The chapter concludes that technology is value-neutral and its worth depends on the context of use — which is what it means for Anakin and Luke, both maimed and prosthetized, to 'bring balance to the Force.'

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 10. On “Crying Like a Bitch”
samples.relation: Roberto Sirvent and Joel Avery read Louie through Kierkegaard's claim that wherever there is contradiction the comical is present: Louie is a walking contradiction - the devoted dad who does masturbation bits - and the show stages incongruities like the homeless man showering behind a subway violinist and the decapitation in an episode called 'Bummer/Blueberries.' Kierkegaard's aesthetic sphere maps both of Louie's failures in 'Something Is Wrong' and 'Moving': the instant-gratification aesthete (the impulse motorcycle, the unaffordable townhouse fantasy) and the overthinking aesthete who cannot break up with his girlfriend or park his car, while his girlfriend shows what it is to actually choose and act. Eddie, who spits abstract truths but does nothing with them, 'plays Hegel to Louie's Kierkegaard,' embodying the gap between abstract philosophizing and lived existence that Kierkegaard attacked in Hegelianism. The closing distinction between irony (spotting the contradiction) and comedy (living with its permanent implications) is what Louis's Conan confession - crying like a bitch and finding happiness rushing in to meet the sadness - gets right.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Nightmares
samples.relation: Auxier asks why the flying monkeys and the shriveling feet of the Wicked Witch of the East give children lifelong nightmares, and answers with a phenomenology of three frightening sequences in escalating duration: the instant shriveling shot, the five-minute cyclone (paired with 'The Great Gig in the Sky' in the Dark Side of the Rainbow sync), and the monkey air-raid. Kierkegaard's Concept of Anxiety supplies the depth psychology: innocence is ignorance, and the child's dreaming spirit projects its own nothing outward, fastening fear onto figures like the monkeys (who are, he notes, played by the Munchkin actors themselves). Merleau-Ponty's lived body versus habit body explains the mechanics: cinema seizes the body's usual 'tour of inspection,' Fleming manipulates active and passive synthesis (the scoreless build-up to the window blow, the barely noticed arsenal of weapons in the Haunted Forest, the dimming lights), and children construct a rigid, inescapable habit body within a single viewing, so the nightmare is the monkey inside our own projected world.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Robert Tally Jr. reads The Graveyard Book as 'spectral existentialism': Bod's climax, 'I'm Nobody Owens. That's who I am,' is Sartre's existence precedes essence made literal, a self made rather than found, and the climactic claiming of the name enacts the self-ownership of the nursery-rhyme pauper 'who nobody owns.' Heidegger supplies the uncanny not-at-home-ness (unheimlich) of the graveyard, which Tally, citing Foucault's 'Of Other Spaces,' calls a heterotopia, while Silas the vampire embodies Lukacs's transcendental homelessness and Kierkegaardian anxiety is transmuted by Bod into the spectral gift of Fear he wields on his bullies. The identity-leeching ghouls named after the Duke of Westminster and the 33rd President are the avatars of bad faith, and the Jacks' attempt to dodge the prophecy fulfills it like Oedipus's, showing that Bod's fate, too, is self-made.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wrathall reads 'Vertigo' through Heidegger's vertigo-before-a-question and Kierkegaard's account of despair as the dizziness of a self whose sensual and spiritual sides are both essential. He uses rock's own testimony - Rammstein's 'Engel' and 'Sehnsucht', Nine Inch Nails' 'Down in It' - to confirm the existentialist thesis that neither flesh nor spirit can be renounced, with Pascal's God-shaped void as the diagnosis. He then argues that 'Beautiful Day', 'When I Look at the World', 'Grace' and 'Mysterious Ways' sketch an existential Christianity in which faith is not propositional confidence but a world-disclosing skill acquired like any know-how, and in which concrete erotic love ('if you want to kiss the sky, better learn how to kneel', the girl with crimson nails who 'has Jesus round her neck') discloses God on earth.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Double Dutch
samples.relation: Krnac explains Holland's five missed penalties against Italy at Euro 2000 — Frank de Boer twice, Kluivert, Stam, Bosvelt — through Kierkegaard's The Concept of Anxiety rather than Cruyff's 'chance' or Vergouw's 'poor preparation'. The self, a synthesis of body, mind and spirit (and of the temporal and eternal), must stake itself on a future-oriented choice, but freedom as 'the possibility to be able' makes every free choice an embrace of the unknown, breeding the anxiety that is 'the dizziness of freedom' — visible in de Boer's slide from a five-out-of-ten miss to a lifeless zero that telegraphed his shot to Toldo. Panenka's 1976 chip shows free action chosen without guarantee, while choosing not to choose is itself an evasion of freedom, in penalties as in life.

samples.book: 106 - Peanuts and Philosophy - You're a Wise Man, Charlie Brown!
samples.title: 7. Life, Liberty and the Pursuit of a Warm Blanket
samples.relation: The chapter explains Linus's blanket via Winnicott's transitional objects, then argues the gang's wider habits - Great Pumpkin taboos, baseball fetishes and rituals - are 'magical thinking' that manufactures an illusion of control over an uncertain world. A middle section tours the mind-body problem (Hippocrates, Descartes's dualism and pineal gland, Huxley's epiphenomenalism, Searle's emergent consciousness) to ask who is really doing the reading. The fallacies section dissects Linus's unfalsifiable Pumpkin doctrine (post hoc after the taboo-breaking 'if') and Charlie's confirmation bias, before reframing his 'pantophobia' as Kierkegaardian angst and Sartrean nausea: with adults reduced to 'Mwaa mwaa mwaa,' the kids are condemned to be free.

samples.book: 216 - The Philosophy of Charlie Kaufman
samples.title: Inconclusive Unscientific Postscript Late Remarks on Kierkegaard and Kaufman
samples.relation: LaRocca pairs Kaufman with Kierkegaard on anxiety as the constitutive human condition—not worry but 'the dizziness of freedom,' the awareness of radical possibility. He argues both use pseudonymity and 'indirect communication' to distance author from work so the audience confronts its own individuality: Kierkegaard's Haufniensis/Climacus, Kaufman's Caden Cotard and the character 'Charlie Kaufman' in Adaptation. The chapter analyzes acting as inhabitation vs. impersonation (Being John Malkovich vs. The Talented Mr. Ripley), the diegesis/mimesis layering (Plato and Aristotle) of Kaufman's doubles and replicas, and repetition/recursion as the Kierkegaardian leap that love, like faith, demands—so 'the end is built into the beginning.'

samples.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
samples.title: 5. Horror Appeals to Our Dual Nature
samples.relation: Allaire and Gehring argue horror works on Kierkegaard's dual nature, the tug-of-war between finitude and infinitude that produces despair: the show's corporeal terrors (the Demogorgon's kills, Barb's decomposing body with a slug in its mouth, Will's tentacle) trigger the fear of mutilation and extinction, while the intelligent Shadow Monster shatters our sense of being unique, echoing Ernest Becker's claim that we build cultural 'armor' against mortality. Using Carroll's paradox of horror and Stephen King's three levels (revulsion, horror, terror), they contend we enjoy confronting these fears safely from the couch, with the Shadow Monster looming over the Snow Ball as an emblem of real horrors, from AIDS to 9/11, still to come.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: The Verdict
samples.relation: Turner runs an ethical audit of iPod use through Levinas's face-to-face: sharing one iPod with his wife forces 'musical justice' negotiations (veto power over a Motörhead cut, gnashing through Bette Midler), his toddler son's listening requires vigilance, and illegal downloading fails Levinas's test that morality begins by ceding 'my place in the sun' to the Other — hence Radiohead's pay-what-you-want release as the Levinasian move, and iPod cafés where strangers DJ for each other while language preserves alterity. Heidegger supplies the counterweight: the shuffle's 'openness to mystery' versus calculative mastery that reduces The Who's Tommy to the 'Pinball Wizard' riff and silences all non-digital media, just as Kant's conditions of possible experience (space, time) would silence things outside them. Derrida's point that categories contain traces of what they exclude illuminates unclassifiable marginal works — bluegrass Pink Floyd, San Francisco Symphony plays Metallica — and the verdict closes with Hölderlin's 'where danger is, grows the saving power also', exiting Plato's cave by thinking the iPod's ethics at all.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: 29 The Dangers of Technology in Black Mirror
samples.relation: Staged as a chatroom of uploaded dead philosophers (itself a Black Museum-style cookie gimmick), the chapter stages the technology debate as Francis Bacon's optimism - technology is neutral, humans mess up, the Grain could educate and MASS could treat PTSD - against Heidegger's claim that technology is a way of thinking that turns everything, including the human mind kept on call behind the Grain and Nosedive's rated behaviors, into a resource. McLuhan's 'the medium is the message,' Benjamin's aura (he recoils at being a reproduction without aura, then a 'limited' Benjamin 2.0 embraces exhibition value and Netflix's reach), Levinas's ethics of the Other against Heidegger's ontology, Arendt's ethic of responsibility born of Nazism, and Ellul's technique - the autonomous totality of efficiency-seeking methods that enslaves us - collide over episodes from The National Anthem to Hated in the Nation, until uploading all the Greek philosophers to recover techne crashes the computer.

samples.book: 181 - Ultimate Lost and Philosophy - Think Together, Die Alone
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Brett Chandler Patterson reads Lost through C. S. Lewis's Chronicles of Narnia as myth rather than allegory - the Lamp Post station and flight 316 (the Prince Caspian dedication page) wink at the source - with the island, like Narnia, a world of crisis and second chances entered by plane crash instead of wardrobe. Flashbacks of past failures (Kate the fugitive, Sayid the torturer, Charlie's addiction, Locke's kidney con) set up struggles for faith that he illuminates with H. Richard Niebuhr on faith as a center of value and revelation as communal, and with Levinas's claim that we become ourselves only through responsibility to the Other in community. The Jack-versus-Locke man-of-science/man-of-faith debate, Charlie's moth-cocoon trial, and Jacob and the Man in Black's black-and-white stone game map onto Aslan versus the White Witch, ending in redemption through the new community and Jack's sacrificial death.

samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 4. Faces from Another Dimension
samples.relation: Hooke frames the volume through Levinas's claim that the face presents itself from a dimension of transcendence, with Kierkegaard's Abraham, Sartre's existential look, and Beauvoir's faces of the elderly and the second sex in the background, plus Lingis on trust. He shows how TZ masks its deadliest figures with trusted faces — Robert Redford as Death in 'Nothing in the Dark,' Sebastian Cabot's avuncular Pip revealing 'This is the other place!' in 'A Nice Place to Visit,' the witch of 'Jess-Belle,' the gentle Kanamits whose book turns out to be a cookbook — so that proof of trust is nearly impossible and the show has us laughing with the Devil. The Turing test is applied to Alicia's tear in 'The Lonely' (clearly in love 'regardless of the organs or hardware beneath'), the slot machine of 'The Fever,' and the aged couple of 'The Trade-Ins,' whose faces silently recognize a lost shared life.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 2. What Does Life Mean after the Snap
samples.relation: This chapter reads four post-Snap Avengers as existentialist answers to how life keeps meaning after catastrophe. Tony Stark embodies Sartre's existence precedes essence, defining himself through free choice up to his final 'I am Iron Man' snap that erases Thanos and his army; the merged Professor Hulk lives Camus's Sisyphus, embracing the absurd and concluding 'all is well' after watching his own past rage; Captain America lives Levinas's ethics of the Other, from refusing to abandon brainwashed Bucky in Civil War to wielding Mjolnir to save Thor; and Ronin-era Hawkeye enacts Nietzschean nihilism until Black Widow's Vormir sacrifice, read through Zarathustra's burning in one's own flame, restores his meaning. The authors conclude Marvel's answer is affirmation: courage to affirm freedom, the Other, and life itself against Thanos as personification of genocide, climate change, and war.

samples.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
samples.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
samples.relation: Spencer gives a phenomenological account of bodily transformation in the films: with Merleau-Ponty, Peter's new body changes his world — walls become surfaces to climb — and grants motor knowledge that needs no calculation, while Norman Osborn's deliberately seized powers feed pride and Doc Ock's grief shows how transformation can sweep a weak will into vice. Virtue, on Aquinas's definition as the perfection of a power, develops only through choices and habits worked out across a whole life, so ethics is deeper than rule-following. With Levinas, the call to goodness is experienced bodily: sympathy with others' suffering draws Peter out of himself — he rushes into a burning building even when powerless in Spider-Man 2 — and the Green Goblin lives a self-contradiction by feigning deafness to it, while eros for Mary Jane both distracts from and ennobles the quest.

samples.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
samples.title: 18. Heaven Is Other People
samples.relation: Treats the show as a theological sitcom whose afterlife (Gen's algorithmic judgment, cubicles, the Jeremy Bearimy timeline) critiques a pop-Christian eschatology of disembodied Heaven and eternal conscious torment while missing the bodily resurrection of Nicene and N.T. Wright's account. Levinas supplies the positive frame: ethics precedes ontology, the face of the Other demands responsibility before any impersonal verdict — which is why Gen's points system 'wouldn't cut it' and why the show's two-shots, Eleanor's spontaneous good acts, and Chidi's 802 yeses to teaching her matter. Bonhoeffer's religionless Christianity completes the reading of Eleanor's repentance, Donna's and Tahani's confessions, and Michael's self-sacrificing Christ figure: salvation comes through intersubjective, grace-infused transformation, so 'Heaven is other people'.

samples.book: 130 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Get an Afterlife
samples.title: 18. Heaven Is Other People
samples.relation: Mayward examines the show's eschatology, arguing its points algorithm critiques the popular picture of Hell as eternal conscious torment, in the lineage of Jonathan Edwards, while missing historic Christian teaching about embodied resurrection. He then reads the series through Levinas, for whom ethics arises in the face-to-face encounter with the Other prior to any impersonal judgment, a structure mirrored in the show's two-shots and in Eleanor's spontaneous good deeds done before she understands them, and through Dietrich Bonhoeffer's 'religionless Christianity', in which Michael's self-sacrifice and the humans' repentance enact responsibility for neighbors without hope of reward. Salvation in the show is intersubjective transformation: where Sartre said Hell is other people, The Good Place suggests Heaven is other people.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Dromm asks what makes Michael's behavior wrong even where the law cannot touch it: as an 'equal-opportunity harasser' of Pam, Ryan, and Oscar, Michael seems to escape Title VII's discrimination requirement. He tests Edmund Wall's 'wrongful communication' definition against the filthy emails, 'that's what she said,' and Michael's solution to the Kevin-Angela dispute in 'Conflict Resolution,' finds it too broad and too dependent on the victim's objection, then turns to MacKinnon's sex-discrimination account and Crosthwaite and Priest's oppression account to explain the distinctive harm to women (pressuring Pam to be a cheerleader in 'Basketball,' calling the party-planning committee his 'bitches'). He concludes that both views are needed, and that in the end harassment wrongs workers by undermining their legitimate expectation of being judged only on job-relevant merit, leaving Dwight's extra effort done for nothing.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 5. The Truth Shall Make Ye Fret
samples.relation: Watson uses The Truth - William de Worde's accidental invention of Ankh-Morpork's first newspaper and the plot to frame Lord Vetinari - to stage the three classic arguments for censorship: direct harm (character assassination 'works every day'), indirect harm (with MacKinnon's point that the speech of the dominant drowns out the subordinated, applied to speciesist insults at Koom Valley), and the false-beliefs argument.
